question.leadin: This Northern Democrat opposed John C. Breckinridge for his party's presidential nomination in 1860.
question.text: Name this "Little Giant" from Illinois who defended popular sovereignty in his Freeport Doctrine.
question.clue: This man was famous for introducing the idea of "popular sovereignty" and was largely responsible for the Compromise of 1850. He engaged in a series of debates with the eventual winner of this election.

swap.text: This slave who frequently had visions led a rebellion in Southampton County, Virginia after witnessing a solar eclipse in 1831.
swap.clue: This leader asked, "Was not Christ crucified?" in response to being questioned if he were mistaken about the circumstances that led him to lead a march on the town of Jerusalem.

question.leadin: "If nominated I will not run; if elected I will not serve."
question.text: Those words were spoken by this Ohioan, in reaction to suggestions that he should be the Republican nominee for president in 1884. He may be more notable for leading the March to the Sea after burning Atlanta.
question.clue: This general sent a telegram offering a captured city to Abraham Lincoln as a Christmas present.

swap.text: This former president was that only presidential candidate.
swap.clue: He appointed Brigham Young as first territorial governor of Utah, which led to the first territorial capital being named after this president.

question.leadin: The highest-ranking Confederate general, Albert Sidney Johnston, was killed during this battle.
question.text: Name this battle, which began after P.G.T. Beauregard launched a surprise attack on Pittsburg Landing.
question.clue: Fought in 1862, the Confederate armies here attempted to drive the Union Army towards Owl Creek, but forces under Grant fell back towards an area that became known as the Hornet's Nest.

swap.text: This person was Lincoln's secretary of State. During Johnson's presidency, he negotiated the purchase of Alaska.
swap.clue: Notable monarchs with this given name include one who was fatally shot by Walter Tirel and one who suffered a postmortem stomach rupture at his funeral due to an incorrectly sized coffin.

question.leadin: The Wisconsin Supreme Court's opinion that a component of this legislation was unconstitutional was overturned by the ruling in Ableman v. Booth.
question.text: Name this legislation that contained a component act ending the slave trade in Washington, D.C. Debates over this legislation featured Daniel Webster's "Seventh of March" speech and William Seward's "Higher Law" speech.
question.clue: James Mason had to deliver the speech written by the ailing John Calhoun against this bill, whose passage was clinched by the support of Daniel Webster and Stephen Douglas.

swap.text: The Confederate forces at Shiloh were initially led by this general, whose death in the battle made him the highest ranking officer on either side to die in the war.
swap.clue: As a colonel, his forces took over for Edmund Alexander and successfully installed Alfred Cumming as governor during the Utah War, in which he camped at the burned-out Fort Bridger.

question.leadin: Name these other Civil War battles.
question.text: By forcing General Pemberton's forces to surrender on July 4th, 1863, after a six-week siege of this city, Grant cut the Confederacy in two.
question.clue: Following the capture of the state capital, John Pemberton was forced to retreat to this city but was unable to harry Union forces after their seizure of the Yazoo River.

swap.text: On the second day of the battle, Confederate troops under James Longstreet attempted to flank the Union army by attacking this hill on the end of Cemetery Ridge.
swap.clue: This hill is where Joshua Chamberlain's bayonet charge drove back the confederate advances as depicted in The Killer Angels.

question.text: This fortification on that covered the southern approach to harbor was attacked in July of 1863 by the , and resulted in the death of Robert Gould Shaw.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the abolition of slavery in the United States.
swap.text: The white abolitionist movement in the northern US was led by reformers like William Lloyd Garrison, and writers like John Greenleaf Whittier and this author of Uncle Tom's Cabin.
swap.clue: Abraham Lincoln reportedly asked this woman if she was "the little woman who wrote the book that started this great war" in reference to her novel Uncle Tom's Cabin.

question.leadin: General Franklin Gardner surrendered Port Hudson after learning about the success of this campaign.
question.text: Name this campaign that saw Lieutenant John C. Pemberton surrender one day after the defeat at Gettysburg. This campaign essentially split the confederacy in half and gave control of the Mississippi River to the Union.
question.clue: An eagle named Old Abe ripped apart rattlesnakes during the downtime of this campaign. The end of this campaign on July 4, 1863 completed the Anaconda Plan.

swap.leadin: In the lead up to this battle, General Beauregard sent a message to Robert Anderson demanding an immediate evacuation of this battle's namesake building.
swap.text: Name this civil war battle which saw future baseball inventor Abner Doubleday defend the namesake structure along with Anderson. Edmund Ruffin fired the first shot at the supply ship Star of the West at this battle.
swap.clue: Batteries at Morris Island and Fort Moultrie fired on the ship Star of the West in the run up to this battle.

question.text: One factor in the migration was this legislation, which promised a 160-acre allotment of land to citizens. This 1862 legislation signed by Abraham Lincoln opened up land in states like Kansas that the Exodusters migrated to.
question.clue: The first person to benefit from this act was Daniel Freeman.

swap.leadin: As a captain during the Mexican-American War, this man led the Ninety Six Guards of the Palmetto Regiment.
swap.text: Name this politician who was angered by a speech that he saw as "a libel on South Carolina" and his cousin Andrew Butler.
swap.clue: This senator from South Carolina famously attacked the author of the "The Crime Against Kansas" speech with a cane.

question.leadin: Name these governors of New York.
question.text: This man was elected in 1872 after working as minister to France and as Lincoln's Treasury Secretary, in which role he ordered that anyone taking down a Union flag in New Orleans was to be shot.
question.clue: This New York governor who, at the beginning of the Civil War, arrested the Maryland legislature. He was appointed Secretary of the Treasury late in Buchanan term.

swap.text: When McClellan did not become the Democratic nominee for governor of Ohio in 1863, the spot went to this man, who conducted his campaign from exile in Ontario.
swap.clue: This Copperhead leader from Ohio wrote the "peace plank" in the Democratic platform. He had been arrested in 1863 after denouncing the war and Lincoln, was sentenced to a military prison, and eventually "deported" to the Confederacy.

question.text: The slogan "Fremont and Jessie Too" was used when John C. Fremont ran for president during this election year, making him the first presidential nominee from the Republican Party.

swap.text: At Mobile Bay, the USS Hartford defeated the Tennessee led by this Confederate admiral who was injured and taken prisoner. He'd earlier been injured captaining the Virginia at Hampton Roads, where he was replaced by Catesby Jones prior to the ironclad showdown with the Monitor.
